plain: Charles Buer says he spent 26 years in electrostatics, the study of static electricity, at a NASA lab at Kennedy Space Center. He says his work showed that brush discharges, a kind of small spreading spark, do not happen in high vacuum, the near-empty conditions of space. He tells it as part of his background in a 2026 interview about a claimed antigravity engine, showing he knows how charge behaves in space.
